notes.drag: carriage drag: none until a source gives one
notes.generation: 4 (inferred): in service from 1984 (generation 3), but the AIM-9M holds section 3570, and its ±40° seeker lies between generation 3's 35° and generation 4's 70° cone (docs/weapons.md §5.1)
notes.power: one hit destroys a fighter (inferred, as the AIM-9M)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; held by blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead (docs/real-weapons.md §1.4) times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (7.4 kg)
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion._spiralAccelBeta: top speed a / beta: 120 / the top speed
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the motion flies the published range from 250 m/s before its flight ends 6 s after the burn (missile.rs real_burn, the rule real_weapons.gd gives the AIM-9M)
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)

footnotes.w-r73: Wikipedia, "R-73 (missile)" (105 kg, 7.4 kg warhead, Mach 2.5, 30 km, cooled IR ±40° (R-73E ±45°)) (read 2026-11-03), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R-73_(missile)
footnotes.ds-aim9: designation-systems.net, "Raytheon AIM-9 Sidewinder" (AIM-9A / B effective kill radius about 9 m), https://www.designation-systems.net/dusrm/m-9.html
